phase5AuditSummary: Phase 5 audit (docs/PHASE5_AUDIT.md): 1.0.0 baseline had zero network layer. Rules engine (src/rules, src/mexe-mode, src/core/rng, src/game-state/store) was already environment-free and reusable server-side. Top risks ranked: full-state broadcast leaking hidden hands, client-supplied card objects enabling forgery, seat-0 rendering assumption, missing revision numbers, client-generated meld ids, AI timers in GameScene, unguarded socket input, stuck lobbies with no reaper, client-choosable deal seeds, and risk of local regression from editing shared files. All ten were addressed in the shared-core/server/client build.

rulesAdaptationAuditSummary: Opus audit (docs/RULES_ADAPTATION_AUDIT.md) found the MVP engine assumed a single 52-card deck with no jokers, ace-low-only runs, sets requiring distinct suits, and a stalemate-by-full-round-of-passes end condition — all four wrong for the final ruleset (two 54-card decks, ace low or high, repeated-suit groups, immediate end on empty pile). It scoped the fix to a nullable-suit/rank Card model with deckId and isJoker, a RulesConfig house-rule surface, and analyzeMeld as the single validity source of truth returning joker assignments, and ranked joker run-assignment correctness and ace-wrap rejection as the top implementation risks.
rulesAdaptationPriorityIssues: validator correctness (analyzeMeld: joker assignment, ace-wrap rejection)
